name: Deafheaven
label: Deathwish
lede: Two friends from Modesto, a demo recorded for $500, and a pink album cover that got black metal argued about in places that never cover it.

eras.title: Two guys from Modesto
eras.text: Two friends who met in ninth grade in Modesto moved to San Francisco and made four songs on a $500 budget. Within a year a Boston hardcore label had them.

years.h: [[George Clarke|7164a191-46a2-41c6-a696-ccb4263e95a0]] and [[Kerry McCoy|23a98713-9978-43b7-989e-625f563f7d20]] start Deafheaven in San Francisco
years.p: The two had played together in the grindcore band Rise of Caligula. The name is a nod to Slowdive.
years.xp:
Clarke and McCoy met in ninth grade in Modesto, California, when McCoy approached Clarke, who was wearing a Slayer shirt in the rain, according to a Red Bull Music Academy interview. They moved to San Francisco in 2010 after Rise of Caligula ran out of direction.

Wikipedia reports that Clarke has said the name is an homage to Slowdive, while acknowledging the phrase also appears in a Shakespeare sonnet.

years.cap: George Clarke of Deafheaven performing live in Barcelona, Spain. · Wikimedia
years.h: A $500 demo, recorded with an acoustic guitar
years.p: Clarke and McCoy cut four songs at Atomic Garden Studios with engineer [[Jack Shirley|54a46dd4-403c-4f54-a12e-351dc9ff9e92]]. They had no electric guitar or amp of their own, so they borrowed gear.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, the untitled demo blended black metal and post-rock, and came out digitally and on limited cassette. The band posted it on a personal Facebook profile literally named Deaf Heaven, and interest came fast.

The Red Bull Music Academy interview says the band had played only eight shows before the label called.

years.h: A five-piece plays its first shows
years.p: Bassist Derek Prine, guitarist Nick Bassett of Whirr and drummer Trevor Deschryver, found on Craigslist, join Clarke and McCoy.

years.h: Deathwish Inc. signs the band after a handful of shows
years.p: [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]]'s label first wanted only to release the demo, then agreed to put out new material too. A 7-inch with "Libertine Dissolves" and "Daedalus" went to webstore customers.
years.xp: McCoy told Red Bull Music Academy he was working at a Ben & Jerry's on Haight and Ashbury when Clarke phoned with the news. Bannon founded Deathwish and sings in [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]].

eras.title: Roads to Judah, and a long way home
eras.text: The first album puts the band on year-end lists. The road takes the original rhythm section.

years.h: Live in a converted loading dock in Bell Gardens
years.p: The January 15 show at The Blacktop is filmed and later released in full as Live at The Blacktop in July 2011.

years.h: Roads to Judah arrives on Deathwish
years.p: Named for San Francisco's N Judah light rail, the debut lands on year-end lists at NPR, Pitchfork and The A.V. Club.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports the record deals with Clarke's year of substance abuse and debauchery. Wikipedia's Sunbather article says Nick Steinhardt of Touche Amore designed both covers.

q: They took us under their wing.
years.h: Touring with Russian Circles
years.p: The Chicago trio takes the young band out on the road for a US run. McCoy later said they "took us under their wing."

years.h: Six weeks in Europe and 3.5 months on the road break up the first lineup
years.p: After a long stretch of touring, drummer Trevor Deschryver quit and bassist Derek Prine left over money trouble.
years.xp: Red Bull Music Academy describes the 2012 European run with Russian Circles as six weeks, part of about three and a half months straight on the road. Wikipedia says early members left over the difficulty of life on the road and earning little to no money.

years.h: Split EP with Bosse-de-Nage on The Flenser
years.p: Deafheaven cover Mogwai's "Punk Rock" and "Cody" from Come On Die Young. A remastered demo vinyl also comes out on Sargent House that year.

years.h: [[Daniel Tracy|c1673fe1-bd6d-42dc-9a07-675106753a68]] takes over the drums
years.p: Nick Bassett leaves and Tracy becomes the drummer, adding his own style to songs Clarke and McCoy had already framed.

eras.title: Pink sky over metal
eras.text: Sunbather makes a metal band the subject of arguments in places that never cover metal. It also makes them a festival act.

years.h: Six days at Atomic Garden to make Sunbather
years.p: Jack Shirley engineers and produces, with Kerry McCoy layering about four guitar tracks per song on a Les Paul.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports the sessions ran roughly eight hours a day, and Tracy tracked most of his drums on day one. Clarke and McCoy wrote the album in their apartment the year before.

years.h: [[Shiv Mehra|94b213fd-9628-49e5-8e10-fbf57e32a589]] and bassist Stephen Clark join for the live band
years.p: The new five-piece takes over touring while Clarke and McCoy remain the songwriters.

years.h: Sunbather: the pink cover and the song "Dream House"
years.p: The eyelid-pink cover by Nick Steinhardt was chosen to match the color you see with your eyes closed in the sun. Pitchfork named it Best New Music.
years.xp:
Metacritic scored it 92 out of 100 from 18 reviews and later called it the best-reviewed major album of 2013, per Wikipedia. It debuted at No. 130 on the Billboard 200, with 3,720 first-week copies reported, and topped year-end metal lists at Pitchfork, Rolling Stone and Stereogum.

The interlude "Please Remember" has Stephane Paut of [[Alcest|dd77b8da-cdc7-46b8-8a7f-10894ca0490e]] reading from Milan Kundera's The Unbearable Lightness of Being.

years.h: The title track, and where the name came from
years.p: Clarke has said the title came from watching a woman sunbathe in a wealthy neighborhood while he was a poor 22-year-old.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, Clarke describes the theme as an unattainable wealthy, beautiful life, and "Windows" pairs a recording of McCoy during a drug purchase with a street preacher. McCoy has spoken publicly about struggling with prescription opioid addiction.

years.h: Metal fans argue about whether it counts
years.p: Traditional black metal listeners dismissed the pairing with shoegaze. The record's success turned the argument into a festival slot.

years.h: First Australian tour, then Between the Buried and Me
years.p: Deafheaven play Australia in January, then support Between the Buried and Me across North America in February and March.

years.h: "From the Kettle Onto the Coil" on Adult Swim
years.p: The single comes out as part of Adult Swim's weekly singles series. Clarke said it followed the Sunbather formula.

years.h: Side projects: Creepers and the label All Black
years.p: Daniel Tracy and Shiv Mehra put out the psychedelic rock album Lush as Creepers on Clarke and Derek Prine's label, All Black Recording Company.

eras.title: Anti- and the long songs
eras.text: The band leaves Deathwish for a bigger label and makes two records about ambition and cost, both at Jack Shirley's studio.

years.h: New Bermuda, the first record on Anti-
years.p: The band recorded it live in April 2015 in Oakland and Palo Alto with Jack Shirley. Pitchfork gave it 9.0, and Spin ranked it first on its 20 best metal albums of 2015.
years.xp: Allison Schulnik painted the cover, an oil painting. Wikipedia says it peaked at No. 63 on the Billboard 200. Clarke told Red Bull Music Academy the pressure gave him night terrors about failing.

years.h: [[Chris Johnson|ddda8caf-1694-49b5-acf8-7b282a5b4954]] becomes the bassist
years.p: He replaces Stephen Clark and is still in the band. Mike Sullivan filled in on bass in 2017.

years.h: Ordinary Corrupt Human Love mixes soft and loud
years.p: Seven tracks, recorded in February 2018 at 25th Street in Oakland. [[Chelsea Wolfe|60e8e938-365e-4429-a141-4c79eb49588d]] sings on "Night People."
years.xp: The title comes from Graham Greene's The End of the Affair, per Wikipedia. Pitchfork gave the album 8.5.

years.cap: Deafheaven performing live at Fete Music Hall in Providence, RI on a cold and... · Wikimedia
years.h: "Honeycomb" gets a Grammy nomination for Best Metal Performance
years.p: The lead single from Ordinary Corrupt Human Love earned the band its first Grammy nomination. Clarke told Billboard the band felt foreign to this world.

eras.title: Just the beauty
eras.text: A B-side, a live-in-studio farewell to a decade, and then the album that drops the screaming.

years.h: "Black Brick" arrives as a B-side
years.p: The single follows Ordinary Corrupt Human Love, per Wikipedia.

years.h: 10 Years Gone, a live-in-studio decade
years.p: The band records its songs live to mark ten years together. The release note thanks fans for sticking with them as they make new music for 2021.
years.xp: Deafheaven recorded Infinite Granite from August to October 2020, at Atomic Garden East in Oakland, Electric Bunker in Boston and Justin Meldal-Johnsen's home studio in Glendale, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: Social media wiped, then a teaser dated 08.20.21
years.p: Two days later the band puts out "Great Mass of Color," with Clarke singing clean instead of screaming.

years.h: Infinite Granite: shoegaze, clean vocals, producer [[Justin Meldal-Johnsen|673f2360-45c1-43d3-b0d2-cf6d798b2fdd]]
years.p: Released on Sargent House, the album leaves black metal mostly behind. The Guardian gave it 5 stars, and Metal Hammer said the band had lost some intensity.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists a Metacritic score of 82 from 21 reviews. Chelsea Jade adds vocals on two tracks. The A.V. Club called it only the beauty, in what it read as a blur of pleasure.

eras.title: Back to the speed
eras.text: A festival takeover, a new label, and an album that puts the screaming back in.

years.h: Roadburn: two nights, two whole albums
years.p: Deafheaven headline the Dutch festival, playing Sunbather in full for its tenth anniversary on one night and Infinite Granite in full on another.
years.xp: Guitarist Shaun Durkan toured with the band in 2023 and 2024, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Deafheaven sign with Roadrunner Records
years.p: The band announces the move to Roadrunner after Sargent House.

years.h: Lonely People with Power brings back the screaming
years.p: Twelve tracks, none over ten minutes, on Roadrunner. "Magnolia" was the first single, with a music video.
years.xp: Consequence named Deafheaven its Heavy Band of the Year for the record. Clarke said on Infinite Granite tours he had to stay still to sing, which did not fit how he wanted to perform.

q: I miss the power and I miss the speed.
years.h: Clarke on why the heavy sound came back
years.p: After the clean-vocal Infinite Granite, Clarke told Consequence why the band wanted to go heavy again.

years.h: McCoy says a new EP is coming, "the heaviest thing we've ever released"
years.p: Kerry McCoy announced plans for the EP in 2026, per Wikipedia.

sources.title: Red Bull Music Academy: Deafheaven interview
